$comment: Layer rules for the arch.imports lane (specs/01-architecture.md sections 3-4). Units are target directories under prototype/src. `files` maps modules that have not moved yet to their target unit by name; delete an entry when its file moves into the unit's directory. `outside` units are not part of the runtime graph: they may import runtime units, and runtime units may not import them.

importOnlyFrom.$comment: specs/01-architecture.md section 6: the core never imports extensions; only the server composition root and the CLI (through each extension's client.ts, see cli below) do.

env.$comment: Direct process.env access, or a read through another env owner the arch.imports parse names (specs/01-architecture.md section 4). The config unit owns the Env port and its process adapter (prototype/src/config/env.ts); every runtime module, the engine (src/server/main.ts), client (src/cli.ts) and memory MCP (mcp/server.ts) entrypoints included, reads the environment through that port. Only the entrypoints listed here may read it directly, each with its justification.

entrypoints.justification: prototype/scripts holds the test runners, gate helpers and test fixtures that npm scripts and the aggregate gate run as their own processes (run-unit-tests, the isolated Dolt fixture, the ACP fixture agent). They sit outside the runtime graph, no runtime module may import them, and each configures itself and its child processes from its environment.

packages.$comment: mysql2 is the Dolt driver. Only store/ (specs/02-data-layer.md section 2) may import it, so no other runtime module can hold a database connection: every read goes through a store reader and every write through journal.commit.
packages.name: mysql2

entrypoints.justification: prototype/scripts/isolated-dolt-fixture.ts starts the isolated Dolt sql-server that the integration and golden lanes run against, probes it for readiness and seeds its fixture rows. It is test tooling that runs as its own process outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

packages.$comment: node:net is the socket API. Only transport/ (prototype/src/transport/node-socket.ts, behind the ByteConnection and SocketHost ports) may import it, so every byte stream the runtime opens goes through the port and no module holds a raw socket.
packages.name: node:net

entrypoints.justification: The isolated Dolt fixture binds a loopback listener on port 0 to pick a free port for its sql-server, then closes it. It is test tooling that the integration lane's runner and the golden harness start outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

packages.$comment: node:child_process starts processes. Only tools/ (the bounded runner in tools/builtin/bounded-process.ts), config/ (the secrets resolver in config/secrets.ts, which sits below tools/ and cannot import it) and runners/acp (the ACP runner) may import it, so every spawn goes through one of those three places. The ACP runner imports it today; the move of the runners narrows this rule to tools/.
packages.name: node:child_process

entrypoints.justification: The ACP runner starts and signals its agent child here. The module has not moved into runners/acp yet (the files map above names it by path, which carries no unit exemption), so it is named until the runners move.

The isolated Dolt fixture runs `dolt init`, applies the schema with `dolt sql` and starts and stops `dolt sql-server`. It is test tooling that the integration lane's runner and the golden harness start outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

The contained Linux target's patch export, run by the operator on the Mac: it starts one fixed `orb` command, with no shell, that runs git format-patch in an executor sandbox inside the isolated machine, and reads its output through a byte cap. It is operator tooling outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

The runtime's entry point on the contained Linux target, which `dyfj-sandbox serve` starts as the runtime role: it starts exactly one child, the server (`src/server/main.ts`) on the same Node executable, with no shell, and forwards its signals and exit status. It is a launcher outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

The deterministic ACP fixture agent, a test agent the fixture profile and the ACP tests start as a child process. On its parent's death it signals its own process group through /bin/kill, and on one test prompt it starts a TERM-ignoring bash descendant. It runs as its own process, outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

The operator's one-off Codex ChatGPT login (`npm run codex-chatgpt-login`) starts the pinned Codex adapter's `login` here, with the runner profile's cleared environment and the terminal inherited. It runs as its own process, outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

The unit, integration and golden lane runners start their node:test files under `node --test` here, and read `node --version` to require Node 26. It is test tooling that runs in the lane runner's own process, outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

Test-lane supervision starts the lane token carrier and the group stop as `node` children of a lane runner, which list processes with `ps` and signal the lane's process group. It is test tooling that runs in the lane runner's own process, outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.
The isolated-Dolt integration lane runner starts the Rust schema round trip under `cargo test`. It runs as its own process, outside the runtime graph, which no runtime module may import.

sqlWrites.$comment: SQL write statements (a string literal beginning INSERT INTO, REPLACE INTO, UPDATE, DELETE FROM, TRUNCATE, table or database DDL, or CALL DOLT_) may appear only in the store's journal, the one mutation path (specs/02-data-layer.md section 2), and in the named entrypoints. The rule sees statements written as literals; SQL assembled from non-literal pieces is out of its reach. The mysql2 confinement above keeps any SQL inside store/, and inside store/ the readers receive only a handle that runs a single SELECT (store/dolt-pool.ts selectOnly), so only the journal holds a write-capable connection.

entrypoints.justification: prototype/scripts/isolated-dolt-fixture.ts seeds the isolated fixture's rows before the lanes that read them start. It writes test data into a throwaway database, not runtime state, and runs outside the runtime graph.
